blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Running a tax calculation accurately is more about discipline than maths. The maths itself is simple: take a number, apply a rule, get a result. The discipline is making sure the number is right, the rule is current, and the result is documented clearly enough that anyone can follow the logic three years from now.

Good teams build a short calculation template for every recurring tax. The template holds the source number, the rule reference, the rate, the calculation, and the final amount. Filling it in takes a little longer than scribbling a number; explaining it later takes a hundred times less.

Tax mistakes are rarely arithmetic. They are almost always in the source number, the wrong rule, or the missing note that would have explained the entry in a future audit.

items.q: According to the text, running a tax calculation accurately depends mostly on…
items.why: "Running a tax calculation accurately is more about discipline than maths."

items.q: What does the calculation template hold?
options: A list of past tax errors
The source number, rule reference, rate, calculation and final amount
items.why: "The template holds the source number, the rule reference, the rate, the calculation, and the final amount."

items.q: According to the text, where do tax mistakes almost always come from?
options: The source number, the wrong rule, or a missing note
items.why: "They are almost always in the source number, the wrong rule, or the missing note."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: If your maths is strong, your calculations will be accurate.
A tax result should be understandable years afterwards.
Documenting a calculation saves time later.
Getting the source number right is critical.
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro argumenta que os erros não são de aritmética, mas de fonte, regra e documentação.

items.q: The line about filling in the template suggests that the author values…
options: speed at the moment of entry over everything else
a small cost now to avoid a large cost later
avoiding templates when time is short
items.why: Inferência: preencher demora um pouco mais agora, mas explicar depois custa cem vezes menos — pequeno custo agora, grande economia depois.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily apresentando o modelo de cálculo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, let me walk you through the template before you start using it. It's one page, and it works the same way for VAT, corporate tax and payroll tax — that's the whole point.

There are five boxes, and they're always filled in the same order. First, the source number — where the figure comes from, with the invoice or the report it's taken from. Second, the rule reference: which regulation or rate table you're using, and the date it was published. This is the box everyone wants to skip, and it's the one the auditor always asks about.

Third, the rate. Fourth, the actual calculation, written out so it can be checked. And fifth, the final amount. Nothing is left in your head; everything is on the page.

Here's my rule for the team. If a junior can pick this up on their first week and fill it in, and an auditor can open it three years from now and follow the logic without calling you, then it works. If either of those fails, the template isn't finished. Take the extra two minutes now — trust me, it pays for itself the first time anyone questions a figure.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does Emily say the template works the same way for VAT, corporate tax and payroll tax?
options: Because juniors cannot handle payroll tax
Because that consistency is the whole point of it
items.why: "It works the same way for VAT, corporate tax and payroll tax — that's the whole point."

items.q: Which box does Emily say everyone wants to skip?
items.why: "the rule reference… This is the box everyone wants to skip, and it's the one the auditor always asks about."

items.q: How does Emily describe the fourth box, the calculation?
options: Written out so it can be checked
items.why: "the actual calculation, written out so it can be checked."

items.q: What does Emily's two-part test (junior and auditor) suggest about a good template?
options: It should change for each type of tax
It should be clear enough to work without her being present
It should be as short as possible even if unclear
It should only be used by experienced staff
items.why: Inferência: se um júnior preenche e um auditor entende três anos depois sem ligar para ela, o modelo se sustenta sozinho.

items.q: What does Emily mean by "it pays for itself the first time anyone questions a figure"?
options: The extra two minutes are recovered when someone challenges the number
The rate must be paid up front
The auditor pays for the template
items.why: Inferência: o tempo investido agora se recupera na primeira vez que alguém contesta um valor e a explicação já está pronta.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Accuracy here is a matter of discipline, not talent." In this context, discipline means…
items.why: Discipline = disciplina: o hábito de trabalhar de forma consistente e cuidadosa.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We use the same one-page ___ for every tax, so nothing is forgotten."
items.why: Template = modelo: a folha padrão que se repete para cada cálculo.

items.q: "VAT is a recurring tax." Recurring means…
options: happening again and again at regular intervals
items.why: Recurring = recorrente: que se repete regularmente.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Always write the ___ next to the figure, so the auditor knows which regulation you applied."
items.why: Rule reference = referência da regra: a regulação ou tabela usada, com a data.

items.q: "Multiply the base by the applicable rate." In a tax context, rate means…
options: the percentage applied to the base
items.why: Rate = alíquota: o percentual aplicado sobre a base de cálculo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre cálculos e auditoria. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The finance manager still has to sign off on every calculation." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new template across all three taxes next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Let's double-check the source number before we file." To double-check means to…
items.why: Double-check = conferir mais uma vez para ter certeza.

items.q: "The auditor flagged up a missing rule reference." To flag up means to…
options: draw attention to it as a problem
items.why: Flag up = apontar, chamar a atenção para algo que precisa ser tratado.

items.q: "A clean template stops small errors from slipping through." To slip through means to…
items.why: Slip through = passar despercebido, escapar sem ser notado.
